articles.title_en: Make a Portable Wide-screen Mechanical TV
articles.summary_en: I never intended to join the cutting edge of electromechanical television. I just wanted to make a nice clock. But sometimes you have to go where the engineering takes you, and in my case it took me to the Scanwheel, a pocket-size wide-screen electromechanical TV with a resolution of 4,096 by 20 pixels. Yup, that’s 4K by 20. The 3D-printed drum [top] is spun by a motor controlled by a driver board [second row, from top]. The driver board, in turn, is controlled by a Raspberry Pi Pico [middle], which also controls the LEDs [second row, from bottom], which are mounted in the 3D-printed casing [bottom] so that the holes pass over them as the drum turns. articles.title_en: IEEE Student Conference Provides Visibility to Budding Authors
articles.summary_en: The IEEE–Eta Kappa Nu (IEEE-HKN) honor society is preparing to host the Innovating the Future event on 6 November. The inaugural one-day, in-person event is designed to provide a forum for IEEE and IEEE-HKN undergraduate and graduate student authors to present their original research papers. A keynote address and thematic presentation sessions are planned as well. Student attendees can network with their peers and gain firsthand experience with the academic publishing process. To present at the conference, students had to submit an abstract of their research before 1 May. Students whose work was accepted were assigned a volunteer IEEE member to mentor them and guide them through the research writing process, including presenting and publishing their original work. articles.title_en: A New NASA Design Turbocharges Nuclear Spacecraft
articles.summary_en: Summary NASA and industry engineers propose a synchronal bimodal nuclear rocket (S‑BNR) to dramatically cut transit times to destinations around the solar system, such as Mars, by combining nuclear thermal and electric propulsion. S‑BNR uses a single reactor with two independent fluid loops and correspondingly optimized fuel zones, eliminating complex mode-switching valves while providing both high thrust and continuous electric power. Major challenges include developing fuel elements that integrate well together, ground testing, nuclear launch safety, and multi-agency collaboration to mature the technology from modeling to in‑space demonstrations. articles.title_en: IBM Built the Cold War’s Most Powerful Code Breaker for the NSA
articles.summary_en: At the height of the Cold War, one very specialized computer was so secret that the world didn’t know it existed. It ran its jobs up to 200 times as fast as any other computer of its time. It was the U.S. National Security Agency’s main cryptographic processor in operation from the time of the Cuban Missile Crisis in 1962 through the Vietnam War and on past the 1975 Helsinki Accords . The machine stopped running only when its moving parts finally gave out. The Harvest computer mattered because of what it was as well as when it ran. For 14 years, it was the engine processing the NSA’s most sensitive intercepts at a time when signals intelligence was as close to a strategic weapon as anything short of a warhead. articles.title_en: AI Companion Robots Are Closing the Human Connection in Modern Homes
articles.summary_en: This article is brought to you by Ollobot . From about 2017, individuals began to truly connect with the initial wave of companion robots. These devices had personality, moved around, joked, and answered when you spoke to them. Most early companion robots, however, were still limited by simple voice-command interactions and narrow functionality. Once the novelty wore off, many ended up sitting unused on shelves. As some of those companies went out of business and turned off their servers, many owners likened it to losing a pet. What Ollobot describes as “gentle intelligence” is a useful way to think about where the serious work in this category is going. Not toward more powerful assistants, but toward more present ones. articles.title_en: Apple TV acquires breakout British hit comedy for global streaming
articles.summary_en: Apple TV has picked up a new comedy series, Small Prophets , for its streaming service in an atypical fashion for the streamer. Rather than commission the project upfront, Apple has bought out the worldwide rights for the series a few months after the show debuted in the UK to record ratings. Small Prophets was the biggest new scripted series launch for the BBC this year, and Apple will be hoping to replicate its success around the world. It streams on Apple TV starting October 7.

articles.title_en: Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra finally dies in bend test, unlike past models [Video]
articles.summary_en: Despite their increasingly-thin designs, Samsung’s foldables have held up well to torture tests that include more bending than you’d ever see in real life. But it seems the Galaxy Z Fold 8 UItra might finally be too thin, as it’s the first mainstream Samsung foldable that’s died in a bend test.

articles.title_en: Private equity bribed Trump $1M, then got $900M for a methane terminal
articles.summary_en: The largest benefactor of the Interior Department’s most recent illegal wind buyout is an Australian-American billionaire whose private equity firm will receive $900 million in exchange for a stake in a methane gas terminal in Louisiana. The near-billion-dollar buyout comes after the same billionaire gave a $1 million bribe to the originator of the deal.

articles.title_en: Wheel-E Podcast: Powerful Bafangs, cops on Sur-Rons, Qronge, more
articles.summary_en: This week on Electrek ’s Wheel-E podcast, we discuss the most popular news stories from the world of electric bikes and other nontraditional electric vehicles. This time, that includes new e-bikes from Flit and SONDORS (yep, that one), testing a battery charging cabinet and the Qronge e-moto, London cops riding Sur-Rons, and more.

articles.title_en: Qronge X1 Spark L Review: Does a $1,299 Sur-Ron Light Bee alternative cut the right corners?
articles.summary_en: If you are late to the pre-teen suburban e-moto scene, we’ve been wading through the exploding market of low-cost Sur-Ron competitors over the past months. While we can all debate the safety and legality issues these bikes bring, the reality is that they are incredibly popular and useful for those who can get around their neighborhoods and back roads and are comfortable hitting speeds up to and above 40mph. Enter the low cost $1299 Qronge X1 Spark L .

articles.title_en: Ontario airport set to spend $5.5 million on electric ground support equipment
articles.summary_en: California’s Ontario International Airport (ONT) has been awarded a $~4.15 million grant from the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) to expand its zero emission infrastructure and add more electric ground support equipment (GSE).
articles.title_th: สนามบินออนแทรีโอทุ่มเงิน 5.5 ล้านดอลลาร์สหรัฐฯ ไปกับอุปกรณ์ไฟฟ้าภาคพื้นดิน
articles.summary_th: สนามบินนานาชาติออนทาริโอ (ONT) ของรัฐแคลิฟอร์เนียได้รับเงินสนับสนุนมูลค่าประมาณ 4.15 ล้านดอลลาร์จากสำนักงานบริหารการบินแห่งชาติ (FAA) เพื่อขยายโครงสร้างพื้นฐานที่ปล่อยมลพิษเป็นศูนย์ และเพิ่มอุปกรณ์สนับสนุนภาคพื้นดินแบบไฟฟ้า (GSE)

articles.title_en: 130-ton electric trucks 4,000 feet beneath the surface of the Earth [video]
articles.summary_en: Swedish mining company LKAB is putting a pair of massive, 130-ton GVW electric Scania haul trucks to work at its Malmberget iron ore mine – which happens to be more than 4,000 feet below the surface of the Earth.
articles.title_th: รถบรรทุกไฟฟ้า 130 ตัน ลึก 4,000 ฟุตใต้พื้นผิวโลก [วิดีโอ]
